sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are as under:

A complaint came to be lodged by the mother of victim girl with Halavagilu police,
Vijayanagara District initially for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.

5. Gist of the complaint averments reveal that on 04.11.2022 at about 8.30 a.m. the victim girl went out of the house in the guise of attending school and did not return even at 1.30 p.m. which is closure of school hours.
Being anxious about non-return of the victim girl to the house, mother of the victim girl enquired her friends and relatives.
Her friends told that the victim girl has not attended the school.
The attempt made by the complainant and her relatives to search the victim girl went in vain.
6. Left with no alternative, she approached the Halavagilu police station on 05.11.2022 at about 8.40 p.m. and lodged the missing complaint.

sentences.text: Police after registering the case, thoroughly investigated the matter.
During the course of investigation, it is revealed that the accused had taken victim girl with him and has dropped the victim girl near the bus stand and from there she called her parents.
She was taken to the police station, wherein her statement was recorded and police came to know that petitioner - accused had physical relationship with victim girl.
Based on such statement, police apprehended the petitioner and filed charge sheet for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC and under Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act.
8. The attempt made by the petitioner to obtain an order of bail is turned down by the learned Special Judge.
Therefore, the petitioner is before this Court.

9. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, learned counsel for the petitioner Sri.Shiva Shirur vehemently contended that the petitioner is innocent of the offences alleged against him and he has been falsely implicated in the case and sought for grant of bail.

10. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the bail grounds stating that the victim girl being aged 15 years 4 months has specifically stated before the police and also before the jurisdictional Magistrate when her statement came to be recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. that the petitioner had sexual intercourse with victim girl and therefore all ingredients to attract the offence alleged against the petitioner are available on record and sought for rejection of petition.
11. Perused the material on record meticulously in view of the rival contentions of the parties.
On such perusal, it is seen that admittedly the victim girl is aged 15 years 4 months and she did not return home on 04.11.2022 as usual.

12. On enquiry made by the complainant with her friends and relatives, she came to know that the victim girl had not attended the school on 04.11.2022 and as the search made by her to trace the victim girl went in vain.
As such, she lodged a complaint with police on 05.11.2022 at about 8.40 p.m.

During the course of investigation, the victim girl called her parents stating that she is near the bus stand and thereafter she was brought to police station wherein she has been enquired by the police and also her statement came to be recorded before the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. wherein the victim girl has stated that the petitioner had intercepted her when she was going to school on 04.11.2022 and took her on his motorcycle and from there he took her to Davanagere and Uchhangidurga and from there to Arebasapur.
He took shelter in the house of his uncle at Arebasapur and they stayed in a room.
At that juncture, the petitioner had sexual relationship with her despite her resistance and he went out of his uncle's house in the guise of attending Aravinkatte and did not return.
13. These aspects of the matter prima facie indicate that the petitioner took the minor girl along with him and had forcible sexual intercourse with her and thereafter left her in lurch.
Prima facie whether at all the petitioner is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the case or not cannot be decided by this Court at this stage by holding a mini trial.

sentences.text:
Suffice to say that the material available on record coupled with the presumption available to the prosecution under Sections 29 and 30 of POCSO Act, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has not made out any ground whatsoever muchless good ground to admit him on bail by resorting to the special powers vested in this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
15.

It is always open for the petitioner to renew his request for grant of bail with successive bail application if there is positive changed circumstance in his case especially after the examination of material witnesses including the victim girl.
16. Reserving such liberty for the petitioner, following order is passed:
ORDER Criminal petition is rejected.
